findings.quote: If the problem does not say the lines are parallel (in words or with matching arrow marks), do not use these rules.
findings.problem: False absolute. Lines can be proven parallel without the problem saying so, and then the corresponding, alternate and same-side rules apply. The lesson's own Core Concept gives two such cases: the reverse rule (one pair of equal corresponding or alternate angles) and two lines perpendicular to the same transversal. A standard item gives one equal pair and asks for another angle; this trap tells the student not to use the rules there. The sentence is carried over from the base wording ('you cannot use corresponding or alternate angle rules'); earlier rounds did not raise it.
findings.source: Checklist B01; reader rules, Added after the Sol audit (test each 'if' rule against a known exception); the lesson's own section The reverse rule

findings.quote: When it cuts two lines, it makes eight angles, four at each crossing.
findings.problem: The lesson defines a transversal only as a line that cuts across two or more lines, without 'at different points', and this sentence now covers any two lines, not only parallel ones as in the base. If two crossing lines and the third line all pass through one point, the third line cuts both lines but there is one crossing and six angles, not eight. The standard definition requires the transversal to meet the lines at different points. Low student harm, but it is a general statement that fails at a boundary case, which the Sol rule grades as a Blocker; the lead may rule on severity.
findings.source: Checklist B01; standard school definition (a transversal intersects two or more coplanar lines at different points, e.g. Jurgensen Geometry; CK-12 Geometry, Parallel and Perpendicular Lines); reader rules, Added after the Sol audit

findings.quote: The letters help your eye. Alternate interior angles sit in the corners of a Z or a backward Z.
findings.problem: This paragraph has five sentences, over the one-to-three limit. Open from round 3.

findings.quote: Corresponding angles sit in matching corners, one inside and one outside the lines. Alternate interior angles are both inside.
